title: Dice, Real Glass, Streamed Type, Detents & Selects
description: CSS random(), glass that refracts the live page, motion for streamed text, dials with real detents, and the native select you can finally style.

drops.title: The Random Is in the Stylesheet
drops.description: Ninety sparkles, forty-four bars and eighty confetti chips placed, coloured and timed entirely by CSS random().
drops.concept: CSS random() moved from spec to shipping this year and the demo run on css-tip.com is what put it in front of everyone. Here it drives a sparkle field, a confetti burst and an equaliser with no JavaScript in the animation path at all — the roll is per element by default, and a --dashed-ident cache key makes a whole row share one value instead, which the last strip demonstrates side by side.
drops.source: Temani Afif · css-tip.com random() demos (Confetti Buttons, Nov 2026)

interaction.mouse: Drag spread, speed and density in the panel; the field and bars re-roll on density change
interaction.click: Click any confetti button to fire its burst
interaction.touch: Everything is tap-driven; the panel hides on narrow screens

drops.title: Glass That Bends the Page Behind It
drops.description: Bento glass tiles that refract the live backdrop through an SVG displacement map, not just blur it.
drops.concept: Apple-style liquid glass arrived on the web this autumn, and the honest version is a displacement filter rather than a blur. Each tile bakes its own map in a canvas from a rounded-rect signed distance field — neutral centre, steep lip at the rim — and feeds it to feDisplacementMap inside backdrop-filter. Rim width, bend and lip steepness are live, and a draggable pill lets you fold a headline in real time.

interaction.mouse: Drag the glass pill over the headline; tune rim, bend, frost and lip in the panel
interaction.click: Grab the pill anywhere inside it
interaction.touch: Pointer events, so dragging works the same under a finger

drops.title: Text That Arrives, Not Text That Appears
drops.description: Three motion policies for generated text: words that settle, a paced reveal that catches up, and a rewrite held for review.
drops.concept: Model output does not land as a finished paragraph — it arrives in tokens at an uneven rate and sometimes rewrites itself. Glyptide names the vocabulary for that (pace, catchUp, flush; transient, persistent, review-bound) and this drop implements one panel per idea, including a word-level LCS diff whose insertions and deletions stay on screen until Accept or Discard.

interaction.mouse: Set pace, settle duration and arrival jitter; toggle catchUp or flush the buffer
interaction.click: Replay the stream, or Accept / Discard the pending rewrite
interaction.touch: Replay and review buttons are full tap targets; the panel hides on phones

drops.title: A Dial That Clicks Into Place
drops.description: Three dials whose spring pulls toward the nearest notch while your flick still carries momentum past a few.
drops.concept: A slider says nothing on the way past; a detented dial reports every step. Angle is continuous during the drag, a spring pulls toward the nearest notch each frame, and releasing hands your momentum to that spring so a fast flick rolls through several notches before settling. Each notch crossed fires a tick: a ring flash and a real navigator.vibrate where the hardware has one.
drops.source: Detent Dial, from the gallery guanmo-ai/ui-moments

interaction.mouse: Drag any dial round; scroll over one to nudge it; tune snap, friction and throw
interaction.click: Focus a dial and use the arrow keys for exact single steps
interaction.touch: Pointer capture means a finger can leave the dial and keep turning it

drops.title: The Native Select, Finally Styleable
drops.description: One <select>, three pickers — a card grid, a swatch matrix and a staggered list — with the form semantics intact.
drops.concept: appearance: base-select is the end of the rebuild-the-dropdown-in-divs era: the browser hands over the rendering of the picker while keeping typeahead, focus handling and the form value. This drop styles ::picker(select), ::picker-icon, option::checkmark and <selectedcontent>, animates entry with @starting-style plus allow-discrete, and guards the whole thing behind @supports so an unsupporting engine simply keeps its native picker.
drops.source: Chrome's "Custom select picker layouts" modern web guidance

interaction.mouse: Open each select to see a grid, a swatch matrix and a staggered list; drag the stagger slider
interaction.click: Pick an option — the live form value under the cards updates
interaction.touch: Native picker behaviour on touch, including the platform sheet where the engine provides one
